coffees.description: This is an uncommon HONEY processed Yirgacheffe coffee from the sub-region of Gedeo, grown and processed by the Koke co-op. They are sorted until they have achieved Grade 1 status. The result of all this care is that you have a flawlessly clean tasting coffee with sweet fruity tastes and aroma. Notes of blueberry and honey blossom flavors in here are very pleasant and a healthy dose of acidity. The other flavors of…

coffees.title: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe Washed Chelchele
coffees.description: Yirgacheffe coffee from the subregion of Chelchele and processed at the Worka mill. This area (Gedeo Zone) grows some of the highest regarded and most expensive Yirgacheffe beans, grown over 6000 feet above sea level. It is one of the most rural remote areas imaginable. 8 hours of dusty, nearly impassable dirt roads with incredible views. Sometimes the coffee has to be packed out with horses because travel is so…

coffees.title: Flores Island
coffees.description: Flores (Floor-ess) is an Indonesian island that has a few years under its belt now for exporting a specialty coffee and is starting to get a name for itself on the map and have bigger production. This is a wet-hulled process, giving it the classic Indonesian character with thick body, smooth low acidity, and slight earthiness. This coffee carries official fair trade organic certification, rainforest alliance…

coffees.title: Guatemala Huehuetenango Waykan
coffees.description: The growing region of Huehuetenango (pronounced way-way-tenango) is on the border of Mexico and is some of our favorite Central American coffee because of its chocolate and nutty tastes. Waykan is a brand name used by one of our importers for their purchases throughout the region as they select the best lots they can find to offer to their clients. This lot of Guatemala caught our attention in particular for two…

coffees.title: Guatemala Natural San Martin
coffees.description: Natural processed coffee out of Guatemala is not something you're likely to find very often, so when this one came on the market, I had to grab it. It's from the Solano family on the Concepcion Buena Vista "Good View" farm in the San Martin region way up in the mountains. This is strictly Yellow Bourbon varietal beans. I really can't say enough good things about this coffee. It's excellent espresso, with a…

coffees.title: Honduras El Cirguelo La Paz Washed
coffees.description: This single farm microlot comes from the southern part of Honduras in La Paz. The farm is El Cirguelo run by Juan Carlos Meza Membreño, and this lot is strictly Typica varietal coffee beans. Roasting it right before the 2nd cracks start is my personal favorite — just a normal, creamy-smooth traditional clean cup of coffee with slight hint of floral, white wine, pear, peach. You can take it into the 2nd cracks where…

coffees.title: India Monsooned Malabar
coffees.description: This is not a coffee that can be traced back to the farm - so whether it is grown organically is uncertain. This coffee tells a story. 18th Century Europe imported coffee from India. The coffee arrived via a 3 month ship’s journey in which the coffee sat on the wooden deck exposed to salt water and rains. When technology improved and the coffee arrived quickly, the Europeans said, “what’s wrong with this coffee? It…

coffees.title: Java Dadar
coffees.description: Most of the Java Island coffee is grown on government estates, but Dadar is a private co-op of farmers, which allows the coffee to be organic certified and rainforest alliance certified. Of course, this comes at a price. Taman Dadar Estate Organic Java is the most expensive coffee grown on the island. "Taman Dadar" means "Flower Garden" and is the nickname for the area. This co-op is in the Eastern side of the…

coffees.title: Java Washed Ganung Patuha
coffees.description: Ganung Patuha is a mountain on the western side of the island, where most Java coffee is grown. 33 farmers in the region contributed to this coffee. They have a symbiotic relationship with Rancabali, a conservation center for animals. This is a fully washed coffee which makes it taste much cleaner than most Indonesian beans. Most Indonesian coffees are wet-hulled (semi-washed), which is what tends to make them…

coffees.title: Kenya Kamathura AB
coffees.description: This lot is selected from various farms and mills throughout Kenya with quality in mind above all else. Kamathura translates directly to "Kamavindi's Selection", named for the family owned business that carefully curated the selections to create this lot from all over Kenya. The Kamavindi Company has existed since 1958 and is committed not only to sourcing great coffees but also to educating farmers on best…

coffees.title: Kenya Kamwangi PB
coffees.description: This coffee is grown by the Kamwangi Farmers Cooperative who operate under the Nyeri umbrella which is the closest thing to Fair Trade Organic that Kenya has right now. The varietals in this lot consist of SL-28 and Ruiru 11 varietal coffees. It is in the Kirinyaga Region, which is on the slopes of Mount Kenya, and one the first places we look when we are shopping for the best Kenya lots. It's a small dense…

coffees.title: Kenya Kiambu AB
coffees.description: From the Kiambu region, and Kiambu is the highest-producing region in Kenya due to its high rainfall and cooler temperatures in the highlands . The climate here is good for growing tea as well as coffee, and they produce a lot of each. The AB sized beans are a blend of the SL-28 and SL-34 varietals that the good Kenyas tend to be. The notes are not your typical bright, grapefruit profile, but rather we are getting…

coffees.title: Kenya Nyeri Ndaroini AA
coffees.description: The Ndaroini washing station is located near the town of Karatina and within the Nyeri region. This lot is sourced from a number of small hold farms throughout the region to maximize quality and consistency. This one has a plum and citrus character character to it and with interesting floral and general winey notes and dark fruit flavor. Crisp and clean and a lingering finish. These are the large AA size beans --…

coffees.title: Nicaragua Jinotega Paraiso
coffees.description: If you’re not familiar with fine Nicaraguan coffee, here’s the rundown: it's normal coffee, or what you might call "mild" because there's nothing jumping out at you. It has surprisingly low acidity for a Central American coffee, subtle undertones of creamy walnut, sweet and pleasant flavor, with a faint milk chocolate aftertaste. Its simplicity allows it to be a very approachable coffee, and in roasting it, it is a…

coffees.title: Peru Cajamarca
coffees.description: Peruvian coffees tend to be cleaner and smoother than the other South American origins. This one is a single farmer microlot in the Cajamarca region, and is comprised of Cattura and Typica varietals. Peru is never terribly interesting, but at a light roast (30-40 seconds past the end of the first cracks) it's got a lot more going on than you would expect. You certainly can roast it dark. It's an above average…

coffees.title: Sumatra Kerinci Natural
coffees.description: These beans come from what would normally be considered Mandheling territory, but it's not grown by Mandehling people, so it's referred to as Kerinci Valley, which is an extremely fertile growing area with a population of around 300,000 people. The Kerinci Valley is known as the "rice bowl" of Sumatra because of all the crops grown there feed some seven million people. This coffee grows near the Kerinci Seblat…

coffees.title: Sumatra Mandheling
coffees.description: This crop of Sumatra Mandheling has all the characteristics you would expect -- low acid, flashes of bitter with sweet, bourbon-like complexity, herbal notes, spice, smooth, rich, not musty, great lingering aftertaste. This is grade 1 Sumatra but don't expect that to mean that the beans will look pretty. Sumatra Mandheling is not sorted by size, and you will find the broken beans and defects that are typical for…

coffees.title: Tanzania Mbozi Mandomashe AA
coffees.description: This coffee is from the Mbozi region, grown by the AMCOS co-op. AMCOS was founded in 2018 when the government started allowing farmers to sell directly to importers and build relationships with buyers instead of selling all coffees through an auction system. The new system encourages quality and provides more financial certainty for the farmer. This particular portion of the co-op 150 farmers who call themselves…

coffees.title: Tanzania Southern Highlands Zanzibar
coffees.description: This is a large lot of Tanzanian Peaberry coffee from a co-op of several farmers in the Southern Highlands. It's not as complex or interesting as a microlot, but it's a really nice coffee for the price. My favorite part is how sweet it is, almost nectar-like. In light roasts you get toffee, green tea, orange, just the right amount of acidity, mild fruitiness without being weird, wonderful aroma, lingering…

coffees.title: Uganda Bugisu
coffees.description: Ugandan coffee is not your “typical African” mug of sweet fruity acidic tones. It is low acid, even mildly earthy and bold tasting in darker roasts. But that doesn’t mean it’s bad coffee!! It’s our #1 best selling coffee, both roasted and unroasted. It's one of my favorite origins to support, and here's why: This Bugisu co-op is an organic certified coffee in Uganda with the most consistent quality control that I…

coffees.title: Vietnam Duc Trong
coffees.description: Vietnam of course isn't really in Indonesia. But it makes sense that coffee can grow here. They have the mountains for it, and they are the second biggest global grower of robusta coffee, so coffee is a big part of their economy. But this is arabica coffee! I suspect none of our customers have had Vietnamese arabica coffee before. This is rare. Women are leading the way in bringing the coffee industry to life in…

coffees.title: Yemen Mokka Natural
coffees.description: Yemen coffees are wild and amazing, rich, hoppy, chocolatey cups that keep you going back for more and more. In general, Yemeni coffee beans are small but produce large amounts of chaff. Depending on your coffee roasting set up, either of these things can cause issues. Expect undertones of baked pumpernickel bread, chocolate, bitter herbs, butterscotch, and spice — a dark sultry spiciness that pairs well with…

coffees.title: Habtamu Danche
coffees.description: This is the green, unroasted version of our Habtamu Danche . This is the year of Habtamu! We roasted this gorgeous washed Ethiopian for our monthly subscribers in July, and now it's available for everyone. Ethiopia is having a banner year, and Habtamu is knocking it out of the park. We're loving this coffee's big, ripe apricot coupled with a touch of pineapple and jasmine-like florals. Habtamu Fikadu Aga is the…

coffees.title: Komothai AB
coffees.description: Komothai AB is a fresh crop Kenyan coffee that recently landed in the roastery. The arrival material barely missed Prodigal's strict cupping threshold, so we're selling it as green instead. This coffee features flavors of orange and cherry, and a bit of the typical Kenyan savoriness. We scored it approximately 87 points. This is a single-estate coffee, which is rare for Kenya. The coffee was also processed and…

coffees.title: Rose Drift
coffees.description: This semi-washed pink bourbon from Finca Buena Vista, run by husband and wife Edgar Motta and Susana Mences, just landed at the roastery! Cherries were picked based on density, depulped, and processed using a semi-washed protocol preserving part of the mucilage. The coffee dried on raised beds in a single layer for 16-22 days. We are tasting berries and citrus with a sparkling acidity and a slight savory quality.…

coffees.title: Burundi Colline Masenga
coffees.description: The profile is on the delicate and bright side for Burundi, with elegant acidity that weaves through complex raw sugar sweetness. Top notes hint at cinnamon stick, rose hips tea, and lemon. Excellent pour-over. City to City+.

coffees.title: Burundi Monge Murambi Hill
coffees.description: Syrupy bodied coffee with clean, bright flavors that are sweet from start to finish. Cane sugar and honey sweetness, hints of English Breakfast tea, orange essence, mouth-cleansing acidity. The complete package! City to Full City.

coffees.title: Burundi Mutambu Migoti Hill
coffees.description: Excellent light roast brew, elegant, bright, with prevalent sweetness, and top note highlights of cherry, raw sugar, spice tea, rose hips, and a twist of lemon. Dark roasts are best for espresso. City to Full City. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Cameroon Kouoptamo Cooperative
coffees.description: The cup is bittersweet and roast-toned, with hints of brown rice syrup, filbert nut, toasted coconut, lemon bars, earthy Matcha. A rare opportunity to try coffee from Cameroon. City+ to Full City+.

coffees.title: Colombia Huila EA Decaf
coffees.description: Sweetly balanced with hints of fruit that lend to a lively acidic impression for decaf coffee. Notes of barley malt, honey, fresh green apple, cinnamon, cocoa powder. City to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Colombia Huila La Argentina
coffees.description: Versatile Colombia, from mid-toned semi-sweet chocolate and tarry burnt sugars, to intense cocoa roast flavors and thick body when roasted dark. Great coffee for milk drinks. City+ to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Colombia Productores de Buesaco
coffees.description: This small producer blend from Buesaco has made such a well-rounded brewed coffee, toffee and creamy caramel sweetness accented by notes of baked apple, pear butter, milk chocolate, and juicy acidity. City to Full City+.

coffees.title: Costa Rica Black Honey Reina Elizabeth
coffees.description: Fruit-accented sweetness in light roasts, agave, dried apricot, fruit tea infusions, rustic cocoa, brisk acidity. Surprisingly syrupy dark roast too, Belgian dark chocolate, cacao nibs, stone fruit. City to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Costa Rica Dry Process Hacienda Sonora
coffees.description: Intense fruit flavors and winey accents should appeal to fans of anaerobic coffees, with impressive sweetness too! Peach brandy, raspberry balsamic, pomegranate molasses, chocolate liqueur, tannic tea. City to Full City.

coffees.title: Costa Rica Honey Process Hacienda Sonora
coffees.description: Pungent bittersweetness connects to interesting accents of fruits and light herbal notes. Canned plums, unsulfured apricot, dark fruits with a winey ripeness, long bittering notes, pronounced body. City+ to Full City+.

coffees.title: Costa Rica Tarrazu Beneficio Los Angeles
coffees.description: The cup intensity comes off a bit like honey process coffee, moderately fruited, round body and rustic-sweetness underneath. Notes of dark corn syrup, dried peach, fig bar, apricot tea, raw nut and carob. City to Full City.

coffees.title: Costa Rica Tarrazu La Casona
coffees.description: Brightly sweet Costa Rica profile, mouth cleansing flavors, molasses, honey graham, barley tea, apple-like acidity, lighter body, nuanced finishing notes of lemon rind and tannic tea. City to Full City.

coffees.title: Costa Rica Tarrazu La Obediencia
coffees.description: Clean sweetness underscores the cup, syrupy like butterscotch and caramel sauce, accented by roast-toned chocolates, silky body, and apple-like acidity. City to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Costa Rica Yellow Honey Helsar de Zarcero
coffees.description: Balanced sweetness, silky body and moderate bright accents. Syrupy texture is punctuated by a flavor of chocolate sauce, with accents of toasted coconut, almond, apple and a spiced finish. City to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Costa Rica Zarcero Monte Brisas Danto
coffees.description: Balanced bittersweetness, hints of burnt caramel, citrus zest, dried raisin, marzipan, chocolate-toned bass flavors when roasted dark, full body, baking chocolate in the finish. City to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: El Salvador Dry Process Cuscatleco
coffees.description: Pungent dark-toned bittering with a range of rustic fruits, and enticing cup aroma. Palm sugar, dried prune, cacao nibs, honey mead, cinnamon bark, cherry wood. City to Full City+.

coffees.title: El Salvador Dry Process Icatu
coffees.description: Pungent dry process with intense bittersweet flavors, countered by rustic fruits and a winey aroma. Notes of fruit leather, preserved orange, toasted sesame, burnt caramel, Sherry, Oaxacan chocolate. City+ to Full City+.

coffees.title: El Salvador Dry Process Miravalles Pacamara
coffees.description: A more fruit-forward, bittersweet profile than the washed Pacamara we sold earlier this year. Intense roast tones, burnt sugar, layered dark cocoa, rustic dried fruits and winey accents, lemon sage aroma, lime zest. City to Full City.

coffees.title: Ethiopia Anaerobic Natural Gerba Dogo
coffees.subregion: Gerba Dogo, Bule Hora, Guji Zone
coffees.description: Ripe fruits are balanced by supportive sweetness and delicate aromatic highlights. Complex profile of berry compote, peach jam, fresh hops, rue, winey accents of oaky rum and fruit liqueur chocolates. City to Full City.

coffees.title: Ethiopia Dry Process Birbirsa
coffees.description: Brightly-accented dry process coffee, with stone fruit and honey notes that are unique to coffees from the West. Red honey, pear, peach, Earl Grey tea, cocoa bittersweets (especially in dark roasts). City to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Ethiopia Dry Process Bobea Uke
coffees.description: Straddles the line between fruit-forward flavors and delicate aromatics, excellent both light and medium roasted. Berry-toned sweetness, passion fruit, dried peach, tea bittering, whole spices, chocolate-covered fruit. City to Full City. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Ethiopia Dry Process Guji Goro
coffees.description: Pairs dry process flavors of expressive fruits and rustic sweetness with the kind of bright acidity and aromatic highlights of a washed coffee . Boysenberry, dried apricot, potpourri, citrus, chocolate-covered fruit. City to Full City.

coffees.title: Ethiopia Dry Process Guji Tuku
coffees.subregion: Gerba Dogo, Bule Hora, Guji Zone
coffees.description: Impressive interplay of potent aromatics and snappy fruits, with fragrant profiles of rose and jasmine pearl teas, lemongrass, rue herb, tart raspberry, orange and pomegranate molasses. City to City+.

coffees.title: Ethiopia Dry Process Kercha Haruse
coffees.description: On the "light and bright" end of the spectrum for dry process coffees, clean fresh fruits, citron essence, yuzu, and mandarin, lightly floral, fragrant black tea. Makes an excellent pour-over brew. City to City+.

coffees.title: Ethiopia Dry Process Korate
coffees.description: Korate shows very nice fruit tones in the cup, with shifting flavor profiles as it cools. Bittersweet tones underpin the cup, with dried peach, berry, mint, baking spices, red tea, pungent burnt sugar, dark chocolate truffle. City to Full City+.

coffees.title: Ethiopia Duromina Aba Bulgu
coffees.description: Syrupy honey sweetness is brightly accented by aromatic fruits and vibrant citrus notes. Accents of juicy stone fruits, ripe strawberry, mango, lemon Italian ice, hibiscus tea. Works well at a range of roast levels. City to Full City.

coffees.title: Ethiopia Guji Hambela Dabaye
coffees.description: Delicious and delicate light roasted, refined sweetness, tart acidity, and fragrant accents. Notes of honey, simple syrup, maple, pear, orange marmalade, and floral hints that permeate the aroma. City to City+.

coffees.title: Ethiopia Uraga Gogogu
coffees.subregion: Wate Gogogu, Uraga Woreda, Guji Zone
coffees.description: Such an expressive coffee that shows excellent cup clarity and fragrant aromatic highlights. Syrupy-sweet cane juice, ginger snap cookie, freesia flowers, hops fruit tea infusions, kiwi and mango. City to Full City.

coffees.title: Ethiopia Uraga Raro Boda
coffees.description: Light and bright coffee, tea-like and aromatic. It pulls out delicate sweetness and mouth cleansing acidity, with notes Earl Grey, jasmine, lemongrass, basil, simple syrup, honey and limeade. City to City+.

coffees.title: Ethiopia Uraga SWP Decaf
coffees.description: Lively decaf coffee, sweetness that's fairly refined, like simple syrup made with brown sugar. Notes of honey, lemon black tea, chocolate malted grain, cherry cordial, and lemongrass in the nose. City to Full City.

coffees.title: Green Coffee Subscription
coffees.description: Take the hassle out of choosing green coffee, and keep up your stash with a selection of our outstanding, carefully selected green coffee. You are able to choose the frequency and amount you receive, and it's easy to change or cancel at any time! The coffees we send are from our extensive inventory of green coffee here at Sweet Maria's. At times they might be coffees exclusive to the sampler set, and not available…

coffees.title: Guatemala Antigua Hunapu Ciudad Vieja
coffees.description: Well-balanced, bittersweet brew, hints of caramel glaze, hazelnut-chocolate spread, and malted beer grains. Moderate acidity points to zested citrus and roasted barley tea. City+ to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Guatemala Antigua La Folie
coffees.description: Good cup clarity, bracing highlights and a sweet, refined finish. Notes of cane sugar, marzipan, tangerine, rose hips, with cocoa undertones that can be developed with roast. City to Full City+.

coffees.title: Guatemala Atitlan Robusta
coffees.description: Pungent bittering and a potent savory dimension, with thick body and low acidity. Notes of cacao nibs, baking chocolate, burnt popcorn, toasted barley, cumin, long bittering finish. Full City to French. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Guatemala Chimaltenango Tecpán
coffees.description: Nutty-sweet impressions and bittersweet at a wide range of roasts. Notes of cocoa-dusted almond, toffee nut, chocolate-covered pistachio, cocoa butter and sesame halva. City+ to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Guatemala El Socorro Java Variety
coffees.description: Delicate flavors, transparent sweetness and aromatic top notes are elegant and refined. Great "Java" character, tea-like, lemon, coriander, rose hips, with bracing acidity that suits the light bodied cup. City to City+.

coffees.title: Guatemala FTO Huehuetenango WP Decaf
coffees.description: Balanced flavors, lightly sweet and malty, capable of deep-toned profiles in dark roasts. Notes of sorghum syrup, malted milk powder, raw almond, baking spice, tea bittering, cocoa. City to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Guatemala Libertad Aurelio Del Cerro
coffees.description: Balanced sweetness and pleasant roast tones are accented by hints of brown sugar, cinnamon, red apple, berry tea, chocolate torte, and more. A very versatile coffee. City to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Guatemala Michicoy Finca Rosma Lot 1
coffees.description: Light roasts brew a sweet undercurrent of raw sugar and light caramel, with hints of dried apple, blackberry leaf tea, cinnamon and malic brightness. Deeper roasts develop bittersweet chocolate tones and raisin. City to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Guatemala Patzun Finca La Florida
coffees.description: Bittersweet core flavors are accented by light citrus hints, lemon bar, marzipan, baking spice. Roast tones take on a chocolaty dimension, especially at medium and dark levels. City to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Guatemala Xinabajul Axel Palacios
coffees.description: Delicious confluence of dark sugars and dried fruit hints, with fruited acidity that has a pleasantly grabby aspect. Notes of brown sugar, dried fig and date, orange tea, dark chocolate truffles. City to Full City+. Good for espresso

coffees.title: Guatemala Xinabajul Rosalio Villatoro
coffees.description: Balanced bittersweetness at a wide range of roasts, with crowd-pleasing flavors of chocolate and nuts. Flavors of toffee, semi-sweet chocolate chips, chocolate biscotti, almond and walnut. City+ to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Hawaii Kona XF Darnall Estate Typica
coffees.description: * Limit 2 lb per customer. Balanced sweetness opens up to subtle bright tones, and top note hints that are elegant and clean. Molasses, burnt sugar, brown malt, rose hips tea, citrus, cola, pleasantly sweet finish. City to City+.

coffees.title: India Monsoon Malabar AA
coffees.description: An interesting cup for fans of earthy, pungent roast tones, and low acid coffees. Dark roasting recommended, brings body and deep low tones to espresso blends (we use it in Liquid Amber!). Read full cup notes. Full City+ to French. Good for espresso blending.

coffees.title: Kenya Kiambu Spike AA Lot 2
coffees.description: Sweetness forward, with well integrated acidity and a sweetly-spiced aroma that lingers in the aftertaste. Notes of maple, blackberry tea, cranberry, goji berry, lemon, tannic tea-like finish. City to Full City.

coffees.title: Kenya Meru Kinjo AB
coffees.description: Leads with rustic sugar sweetness in the cup, cooling to moderate hints of fruits and well-integrated acidity. Date sugar, molasses, canned plum, bittering tea and cocoa finish. City to Full City. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Kenya Nyeri Gaikundo AA
coffees.description: Raw sugar sweetness and mouth refreshing acidity lie at the heart of Gaikundo's cup profile, with pronounced flavors of raw sugars, high-toned citrus accents, orange, grapefruit, and tart rose hips tea. City to City+.

coffees.title: Kenya Nyeri Igutha AB
coffees.description: Pour-overs are a real treat, with bright fruits and tangy accents that feel well integrated into the cup sweetness, and an aromatic top end. P iloncillo sugar, orange, green apple, tamarind, Earl Grey, cardamom . City to Full City.

coffees.title: Kenya Nyeri Igutha Peaberry
coffees.description: Cup sweetness is brightly accented by notes of citrus and spices that feel fairly well balanced for Kenyan coffee. Profiles of brown sugar, lemon, golden raisin, spiced sodas like Dr Pepper, tea bittering finish. City to City+.

coffees.title: Kenya Nyeri Kaiguri AA
coffees.description: Sweetness-driven Kenya that's not all high tones. A middle ground between layered raw sugars and brightly accented hints of citrus and black tea. Makes a great chocolate-laden dark roast too. City to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Kenya Nyeri Kamoini Peaberry
coffees.description: This juicy peaberry lot is underscored by plump fruit and berry notes, with spiced aromatics and a bright acidic snap. Notes of black currant, grapefruit, tangy plum, cranberry lemonade, Allspice. City to Full City.

coffees.title: Kenya Nyeri Mahiga AB
coffees.description: Tartly sweet flavors are overlaid with spiced complexity and bright fruits. Notes of currant juice, cranberry sauce, Darjeeling and Orange spice teas, cardamom, fragrant lemongrass, mulled juice. City to Full City.

coffees.title: Kenya Nyeri Mutheka AB
coffees.description: Light roasts satisfied our taste for a brightly-sweet Kenya's, and Full City proved to brew a standout espresso. Juicy texture, apple, pomegranate, Turkish Delight candies and brown sugar. City to Full City. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Kenya Nyeri Rukira AA
coffees.description: Aromatic cup flavors and juicy accents are highlighted in light roasts. The sweetness is marked by complex notes of b erry, pomegranate, tangy citrus, vanilla and a fragrant finish that's tannic and tea-like. City to City+.

coffees.title: Mexico Chiapas La Ramona
coffees.description: Ticks off the boxes of a crowd-pleasing brew - balanced sweetness, nutty hints, with modest acidity and dark-toned cocoa. Hints of malt syrup, toffee almond, lemon tea, bittersweet cocoa. City to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Mexico Tenejapa Valle de Jovel
coffees.description: Balanced profile with restrained sweetness of unrefined sugars, hefty cocoa roast flavors, accents of loose leaf tea and walnut oil, hints of apple and smoked chocolate. City to Full City+.

coffees.title: Nicaragua Buenos Aires Maracaturra
coffees.description: City+ splits the difference between subtle aromatics and fully fleshed out sweetness that comes with a bit more roast development. Notes of brown sugar, Assam tea, marzipan, and clove. City to Full City.

coffees.title: Nicaragua Los Alpes
coffees.description: This Caturra lot from Los Alpes is well-rounded and crowd-pleasing, with the kind of bittersweet profile that's great as black coffee, or paired with cream. Brown sugar, almond, Dutch cocoa, apple. City to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Nicaragua Maracaturra Los Medios
coffees.description: This medium-sized bean separation of Maracaturra carries the same delicate aromatic aspects of its larger counterpart, with an underlay of caramel sweetness, baking spice, lemongrass and herbal accents. City to Full City.

coffees.title: Rwanda Nyamasheke Gatare
coffees.description: Aromatic sweetness of caramel and baking spice, with a light citrus oil note that plays into the acidic impression. Hints of brown sugar, pear, cinnamon roll, and a shimmer of sweat tea. City to Full City. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Set: Espresso Green Coffee Sampler
coffees.description: Our sample sets offer broad selection and big savings, perfect for those new to home coffee roasting and seasoned veterans alike! Starting off with a sample set is an economical way to try coffees from around the world, and explore different flavors with just 1 click. No need to do all the research either, we do that for you, grouping together coffees that are relatively easy to roast from distinct growing regions.…

coffees.title: Set: Fruit Basket Flavor Set
coffees.description: Fruit flavors are the theme, featuring coffees that exemplify the many ways fruity notes manifest in coffee flavor profiles. This set includes 1 lb each from four different origins, and often different process methods, all at a discounted price!

coffees.title: Set: Latest Coffee Additions
coffees.description: Our "Latest Additions" coffee set gets you 1 lb bags of all our latest listings. No jumping back and forth between different records to add them to your shopping cart. Simply click the "Add to Cart" button and you're on your way. It's that simple!

coffees.title: Set: Mini Green Coffee Sampler
coffees.description: Our Mini Sample Set includes 4 different coffees in 1/2 lb bags. Our sample sets offer broad selection and big savings, perfect for those new to home coffee roasting and seasoned veterans alike! Sample sets are an economical way to try coffees from around the world, explore different flavors, and discover different processing methods with a simple 1 click "Add to Cart." No need to do all the research either, we do…

coffees.title: Set: Regular Green Coffee Sampler
coffees.description: Our sample sets offer broad selection and big savings, perfect for those new to home coffee roasting and seasoned veterans alike! Starting off with a sample set is an economical way to try coffees from around the world, and explore different flavors with just 1 click. No need to do all the research either, we do that for you, grouping together coffees that are relatively easy to roast from distinct growing regions.…

coffees.title: Sumatra Aged Lintong - 5 Year Vintage
coffees.description: Aged coffees yield intensely rustic flavors that tend to please the wet hulled coffee crowd. Earthy aroma, pungent bittering, brown spices, tobacco, cedar, pepper cask, thick body, and more. City+ to French. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Sumatra Anaerobic Washed Bebesen Aulia
coffees.description: For anaerobic coffee, this lot packs more bittersweet intensity than fruit. Brews balanced flavors and thick body, pungent roast tones, bean to bar chocolate, tannic tea, very long finish. City+ to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Sumatra Giling Basah Sesongot
coffees.description: Rustic sweetness and incredible depth of flavor, with notes of rice syrup, pungent earth-tones, bittersweet intensity, accents of sweet grains and fruit, herbal aroma, foresty finish. City+ to French. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Sumatra Wet Hulled Aceh Tengah
coffees.description: Rustic earth-toned coffee, intense, brown rice syrup, alder incense, pine resin, tarragon, musky fruit hint, dense bittersweetness helps consolidate the flavors. Best with 48+ hours rest. City+ to French. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Sweet Maria's 10 Speed Blend
coffees.description: Celebrating classic lines and versatility of the 10 Speed bicycle, this blend offers classic-toned flavors bittersweet and bright, and is extremely versatile in roasting and brew methods, including espresso. You could say it works great on all gears! City to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Sweet Maria's Altiplano Blend
coffees.description: Highlights the versatility of Central American coffees, balanced bittersweets, well-integrated acidity, rich chocolate, carbonized sugars, hints of nut and citrus. Blended with espresso in mind, but excellent brewed too. City+ to Full City+. Great for espresso

coffees.title: Sweet Maria's Espresso Monkey Blend
coffees.description: We blend this for body, balance between high and low tones, fruited-chocolate, slightly rustic fruit. Good espresso.

coffees.title: Sweet Maria's Ethiopiques Version 2.0
coffees.description: Velvety-textured shot, bittersweet and fruited, with a long lasting finish. Chocolate coated berry, raspberry laced truffles, hints of citrus, spiced cocoa, and creamy chocolate ganache. Full City to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Sweet Maria's Liquid Amber Espresso Blend
coffees.description: A potent blend for espresso beverages, and ideal for milk drinks. Caramel sweetness turns pleasingly pungent; bittering spice, cacao, dark cocoa, savory notes, long aftertaste. Monsoon coffee and a small percentage of Robusta add crema and body. Full City+ to French roast. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Sweet Maria's Moka Kadir Blend
coffees.description: The all dry process Moka Kadir blend offers an underpinning of rich chocolate low tones, rustic palm sugar-type sweetness, earthy dried fruits, velvety mouthfeel, and finishing hints that are bittersweet and leathery. Full City to French. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Sweet Maria's New Classic Espresso
coffees.description: A classic, balanced espresso, but without the baggage of the old world espresso conventions... and without robusta!

coffees.title: Sweet Maria's Strange Beasts Espresso Blend
coffees.description: An unlikely coffee alliance yields balanced bittersweetness, well-integrated hints of fruit, baked goods, molasses, spice, and chocolate almond. Classic-toned, with velvety texture. Excellent straight or in milk drinks. Full City to French. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Tanzania Mbozi Songwe AA
coffees.description: Very nice cup clarity, layered sweetness, and vivid, tea-like acidity. Shows an array of raw sugar flavors, accents of dried fruit and fragrant spices, and a brisk, mouth-cleansing finish. City to Full City.

coffees.title: Uganda "Alpha" Commercial Grade Coffee
coffees.description: An opportunity to explore another side of coffee, infinitely interesting to see and taste. Earthy / root-like flavors with a touch of rustic sweetness, molasses, intensely bittering and pungent, roasted grains, chicory spice, cooked veggies. City+ to Full City+. *Limit 1 lb per customer.

coffees.title: Uganda Dry Process Bugoye Muramba
coffees.description: Intense dry process coffee, pungent roast tones, rustic sweetness, accents of prune, blackberry wine, honey mead, rustic dark chocolate, syrupy body, woody whole spices in the long finish. City to Full City+.

coffees.title: Uganda Dry Process Masaka Robusta
coffees.description: Intense flavors, unsweetened baking chocolate, sharp cocoa, toasted grains, puffed wheat, roasted corn, chocolate beer malt, bitter clove oil, dried tarragon, low acidity. Full City to French. Good for espresso blending.

coffees.title: Uganda Kapchorwa Kabeywa
coffees.description: Light roasts brew balanced sweetness and structured flavors. Sweet notes of creamy caramel, dark toffee, and raw sugar, along with hints of lemon and dried goji berry that highlight acidity. City to City+.

coffees.title: Uganda Yellow Honey Kabeywa
coffees.description: Medium roasts brew bittersweet roast tones, buoyant body and a hint of acidity that brings a structured feel to the cup. Molasses, bran muffin, dark cocoa, aromatic wood, corn silk tea. City+ to Full City+. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Yemen Khulani Amer
coffees.description: Fruit-accented profiles, intensely rustic and bittersweet coffee, notes of dark corn syrup, toasted grain, pumpkin bread, freeze dried fruit, leather, Cumin, bittering chocolate. City+ to French. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Yemen Mokha Haimi
coffees.subregion: Haima Dakhliya, and Kharijea Districts, Sana'a governorate
coffees.description: Baking spice notes make a strong showing, along with classic Yemeni flavors that are deep toned, earthy, and appropriately rustic. Fenugreek, saffron cookie, sesame oil, tangy roast flavors. City+ to French. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Yemen Mokha Hajjah
coffees.subregion: Bani Awam and Mabyan Districts, Hajjah Governorate
coffees.description: Rustic sweetness and deep-toned flavors, with thick body that suits the pungent cup character. Molasses, rye, caramel popcorn, sesame chocolate, baking cocoa, tobacco, cedar chips. City+ to French. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Yemen Mokha Sanani
coffees.description: Intensely rustic, bittersweet flavors, lightly fruited, with body that's about as thick as coffee gets. Barley malt syrup, earthy dark chocolate, natural dried fruits, saffron cookie, fragrant wood and spices. City+ to French. Good for espresso.

coffees.title: Brazil Lagoinha Farm Yellow Bourbon
coffees.description: A beautifully selected Yellow Bourbon from Lagoinha Farm in Brazil, showcasing the naturally sweet and balanced character for which Brazilian specialty coffees are known. This coffee offers a smooth, rounded cup with a pleasant sweetness, approachable acidity and a rich, satisfying mouthfeel. A great choice for coffee drinkers who enjoy a classic Brazilian profile with added complexity and refinement.

coffees.title: Brazil Nossa Senhora da Medalha Natural
coffees.description: This yellow catuai lot comes to us from one of De La Finca's partner farmers: Bruno Henrique. Bruno has done a stellar job creating a cup that is lively and bright, rich and creamy and super clean. We noted green grape, key lime, honey, clementine and baker's chocolate.

coffees.title: Colombia DECAF Natural
coffees.description: It's sweet, fruity and refreshingly clean with juicy notes of blueberry, strawberry, mango, lime and clementine. A real fruit bomb!

coffees.title: Colombia EA Decaf
coffees.description: This coffee is produced by two coffee growers' cooperatives that bring together more than 240 families in the Planadas and Gaitania areas. Each farmer owns between 2 and 4 hectares. These terroirs are protected areas for these indigenous peoples, with more than 6,000 trees per hectare. This coffee has been decaffeinated at the Decaf factory in Manizales, Colombia, using the Sugar Cane Decaf process. This…

coffees.title: Colombia El Porvenir 92 hr Fermentation Parainema Microlot
coffees.description: This Natural Castillo from Finca El Porvenir in Totoró, Cauca, reflects the bold spirit of its origin. Grown at high altitude and carefully harvested by producer Óscar Realpe, this coffee undergoes a prolonged fermentation that amplifies its intensity. The result is a vibrant cup bursting with ripe fruit, tropical sweetness, and wine-like depth. A testament to elevation, precision, and passion. Grown by Oscar…

coffees.title: Colombia Finca La Manoa Geisha Double Washed
coffees.description: José Edwin is a young producer with big dreams. Working under his father's mentorship, he purchased Finca La Manoa and is already making waves with innovative processing techniques. For this Geisha lot, he double fermented the coffee in order to develop and balance the florals and acidity, then double washed it for clarity. The result is a super clean cup with zesty tangerine and lime brightness and a bouquet of…

coffees.title: Colombia Finca La Riviera Sudan Rume Natural
coffees.description: From Finca La Riviera and Finca Milan, this one was declared the unanimous favorite! Sudan Rume is a heirloom variety that predates Bourbon and Typica. When naturally processed, it tastes like a combination of Ethiopian coffee and Yemeni coffee - sweet, fruity yet complex with old world depth. We got notes of strawberry, sangria, lemonade and a bouquet of florals along with a touch of maple syrup.

coffees.title: Colombia Finca Las Nubes Pink Bourbon
coffees.description: Step into the world of Colombia Finca Las Nubes Pink Bourbon from Claudia Samboni, where elegance meets complexity in every cup. Sourced from the pristine highlands of Colombia, this Pink Bourbon varietal delivers an unforgettable tasting experience—bright, vibrant, and layered with nuanced sweetness.

coffees.title: Colombia Honey Aponte
coffees.description: From the high-altitude mountains of Aponte, Nariño, Colombia, this exceptional Honey-Processed coffee is produced by smallholder indigenous growers working at elevations between 1,700 and 2,100 meters. The Honey process brings together the clarity of a washed coffee with the sweetness and fruit character often associated with natural processing. In the cup, expect a bright and juicy profile with notes of…

coffees.title: Colombia Nasa Wesx Yuppie Natural
coffees.description: This coffee comes to us through a partnership between Belco Coffee and the Young Professional People (lovingly called "Yuppies") of the indigenous Nasa Wesx people. They took a big swing by carefully naturally processing this lot and we'd say they knocked it out of the park. It's sweet, fruity and refreshingly clean with juicy notes of blueberry, strawberry, mango, lime and clementine. A real fruit bomb!

coffees.title: Colombia Organic FCC Ucumari
coffees.description: Between the western and central mountain ranges of Colombia, the coffee from Cajibío, Cauca captures the spirit of resilience and regeneration. Produced by smallholder farmers of the Federación Campesina del Cauca (FCC), this coffee represents more than exceptional flavor and tells the story of a community rebuilding peace and prosperity through sustainable farming. In the Puenza Valley, volcanic Andisoles soils…

coffees.title: Colombia Sierra Nevada Finca La Esperanza
coffees.description: This exclusively Castillo variety selection comes to us from farmers Dario and Iliana Delgado and their farm, La Esperanza. Castillo is now the most common coffee variety grown in Colombia because of its resistance to leaf rust and is hybrid of Caturra and Timor. You still get a classic Colombian profile in the cup: it's got rich body, creamy texture, big chocolaty notes, and a walnut undertone. It's subtly bright…

coffees.title: Colombia Tolima Finca La Leona Caturra
coffees.description: Located in the Planadas region of South Tolima, Finca La Leona is owned and managed by Laura Enciso and her father, Don Afranio Enciso. Together they've overcome tragedy, enjoyed triumphs and built a family business that's truly inspiring. This lot features their caturra variety and makes for a perfect daily driver. Rich, bold, balanced, creamy and clean, it's got big notes of milk chocolate and caramel with a dash…

coffees.title: Colombia Tres Amores Microlot Blend
coffees.description: Tres Amores is a blend of GEISHA, PINK BOURBON and TABI. Of the farm's 43 hectares, 25 are dedicated to growing coffee. The farm is managed by Laura Enciso, who has been in charge since 2019. The management of the farm is exemplary, with very little use of products, only when necessary to protect the coffee trees from rust and coffee borers. What is a "WOMEN COFFEE" at Belco? We have decided to support women…

coffees.title: Costa Rica Santa Maria de Dota El Vapor Natural
coffees.description: It's back!! It consists of carefully sorted cherries from the caturra and bourbon arabica varieties grown in the El Vapor micro-region of Tarrazu. While some naturally processed coffees give us a fresh fruit vibe, this cup gives us more of a candied fruit feel kinda like jolly ranchers! We got notes of cherry candy, pomegranate juice, dried berries and caramel.

coffees.title: El Salvador Cerro El Tigre Bourbon
coffees.description: In the shadow of Cerro el Tigre, an inactive volcano, you'll find Maria Cristina Llach's farm. For this microlot, she chose a blend of orange and red bourbon and the result is a luxurious brew - dessert in a cup. It's super rich with a velvety body and big notes of dark chocolate, cashew butter, caramel and cherry.

coffees.title: El Salvador Divina Natural
coffees.description: Roberto Ulloa is driven by an unstoppable passion to produce high quality coffees. His coffee, which scored first place at the 2020 Cup of Excellence, is unparalleled. This Natural lot is sweet and fruity with stone fruit, honey and berries. Coffee is selectively handpicked and processed on Roberto’s farm. Once picked, ripe, red cherry is laid on raised drying beds. Cherry is turned frequently to ensure even…

coffees.title: El Salvador Picacho Superior
coffees.description: The Holman family has been producing coffee in Apaneca-Ilamatepec for over 120 years. They expanded on their initial property, Finca Santa Isabel, by purchasing Finca San Blas and Finca Antioquita. Today, owner Jeff Holman continues his family tradition of coffee farming with a focus on protecting the environment through the farms’ Rainforest Alliance certifications. The composition of each lot varies but is…

coffees.title: Ethiopia Daye Bensa Natural Sidama ARD
coffees.description: Daye Bensa is a big name in the Sidama region and they work with lots of smallholder farmers in the area, but this microlot comes directly from the founder's personal farm. Asefa Dukamo manages mountains of coffee, but this one warranted personal attention - only a handful of boxes made the cut and each one is serialized. It brews up crystal clean, surprisingly sweet and bursting with a bouquet of florals. The…

coffees.title: Ethiopia Kochere Bonde Yeast Fermentation
coffees.description: If you're new to yeast fermented coffee, I can assure you this coffee doesn't taste at all "yeasty"! All yeast does is make coffee's normal fermentation process more controlled and focused. This Grade 1 Kochere is a perfect example: super clean, floral and tea-like with a dash of vanilla and passion fruit sweetness.

coffees.title: Ethiopia Sidama Worku Buche Washed Decaf
coffees.description: This fully washed decaf was hand selected by Worku Buche at his Kadela washing station in Sidama's Arroresa district. It's balanced, clean and gently bright. Along with a lovely floral tone we noted plum, cinnamon and warm vanilla. It's a tasty treat on a cool fall evening!

coffees.title: Ethiopia Washed YirgZ
coffees.description: Yirg refers to Yirgacheffe and Z indicates the minimal to zero defects present in the coffee. Keffa employs a method of triple sorting by size, color, and then density. This additional sorting not only benefits the end cup result but also the producer's staff, as they are paid more for the intense sorting process. While coffees from Ethiopia are typically naturally processed, this washed process gives us a better…

coffees.title: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe Wush Wush 96 Hour Anaerobic Natural
coffees.description: This microlot from renowned coffee expert Israel Degafa comes from producers in Yirgacheffe. At his washing station, Israel uses a proprietary anaerobic fermentation protocol he's dubbed "alcoholic" due to the crisp, winey cups it produces. It's also juicy and sweet with big notes of strawberry, blackberry, banana, lemonade and pure cane sugar.

coffees.title: Guatemala Huehuetenango Rolando Sanchez
coffees.description: There's a specific flavor profile we look for when we source Huehuetenangos, and this single farm offering from Rolando Sanchez's Finca Claima checks all the boxes. It's big and bold with a rich, buttery texture and just a drop of earthy depth. We tasted notes of dark chocolate, caramel, peach and cashew butter.

coffees.title: Guatemala San Marcos Finca Las Lomas
coffees.description: The San Marcos region may not have the name recognition of its neighboring regions, but I'd put this cup against a Huehuetenango any day! This bold, rich and velvety beauty comes to us from the Aguirre family at Finca Las Lomas and it's got "daily driver" written all over it. In our cups, we got rich chocolate notes, complemented by hints of floral and citrus accents.

coffees.title: Honduras Comayagua Santa Lucia Reserve Organic
coffees.description: Captain's Gold top 6! This direct trade coffee from third generation coffee producer Raul Rodriguez is an instant classic. Rich and bold with a buttery texture, it's perfect for your daily driver cup whether it's for filter brew or espresso. It's got a real Sunday breakfast feel with notes of dark chocolate, maple syrup, walnut and a touch of nectarine. Pancakes and bacon, anyone?

coffees.title: Honduras Don Abel Botijas Pacamara Natural
coffees.description: Abel and his family handle every step of production themselves, ensuring consistency and care. Their hands-on approach has made Las Botijas a favorite among roasters who value traceability and flavor integrity. 2021 Good Food Award winner and 2018 Cup of Excellence finalist Two-Time National Champion – The Best of Honduras Late Harvest (Project Origin) 2016– 1st Place 2017 – 1st Place Organized by Project Origin in…

coffees.title: Honduras Don Abel Botijas Pacamara Washed
coffees.description: The farm Las Botijas is named so after the town legend about a hidden treasure buried underground. The “botijas” is a potbellied earthenware jug with two openings used to hide money underground away from humidity, and they were later dug up and used as musical instruments in the 19th century. The coffee farm Las Botijas was purchased by Abel Giron in 2011, and he chose to plant the pacamara variety simply because…

coffees.title: Honduras Finca La Esmeralda 19 Hour Anaerobic Natural Organic
coffees.description: Back after almost two seasons. This direct trade offering comes to us from De La Finca’s new project farm in the Comayagua region of Honduras. Their goal with Finca la Esmeralda is to continually refine their experimental processing so we choose a 19 hour double fermented anaerobic natural! This selection is fresh and juicy with big notes of watermelon, grape, raspberry, and honeydew. It's fruity and fun while…

coffees.title: Honduras Finca La Esmeralda 72 Hour Anaerobic Natural Organic
coffees.description: It’s back from our farms to your homes. Honduras Esmeralda Natural 72 Hours. Sweeter, fruitier, and more vibrant, while still remaining clean and balanced without the overpowering vinegar-like flavors sometimes found in extended fermentations. Our 72-hour natural process begins with carefully hand-picked ripe cherries grown in the mountains of Honduras. After harvesting, the cherries are sorted and floated to…

coffees.title: Honduras Finca La Esmeralda Anaerobic Red Honey Organic
coffees.description: This direct trade microlot comes to us from De La Finca’s newest project farm, Finca La Esmeralda, in the Comayagua region of Honduras. This Anaerobic Red Honey lot was hand selected from their caturra and typica harvest specifically for honey processing in order to offer a cup balanced between the intensity of natural and the smooth cleanliness of fully washed. The cup is clean with notes of lemonade, tropical…

coffees.title: Honduras Lucia Estate Geisha Organic Lot 2
coffees.description: Discover something NEW and truly special from our farms: Organic Geisha , harvested in an extremely limited micro-lot. We are really excited about this one. This would be our 2nd of the season and expecting maybe one more after this. This offering delivers the elegance Geisha is known for bright floral aromatics, silky body, and a refined sweetness. Expect vibrant notes of jasmine, white grape, and citrus…

coffees.title: Honduras Marcala 92 Hour Double Ferment Anaerobic Natural
coffees.description: This Yellow Bourbon from Honduras courtesy of De La Finca Importers is direct trade, organic and bird friendly. De La Finca's 92 hour anaerobic fermentation was carefully developed to give their coffees juicy sweetness without introducing any harsh, vinegary flavors. The result is a sweet, clean cup that's full-bodied with a creamy texture and big notes of raspberry, grape juice, strawberry and watermelon.

coffees.title: Honduras Marcala Black Honey
coffees.description: In 2019, De La Finca purchased a small 9-acre farm on the outskirts of Marcala, La Paz, the hub of specialty coffee in Honduras. Bought specifically as an experimental farm, separate from the family farms in Comayagua, it gives us room to push processing methods and build best practices without risk to our core production. Marcala's elevation and climate make it well-suited to Bourbon, a variety known for its…

coffees.title: Honduras Marcala Red Honey
coffees.description: This Yellow Bourbon from Honduras courtesy of De La Finca Importers is direct trade. De La Finca's Red Honey was carefully developed to give their coffees juicy sweetness without introducing any harsh, vinegary flavors. The result is a sweet, clean cup that's full-bodied with a creamy texture and notes of mango, ripe fruit & cocoa powder.

coffees.title: Jairo Arcila Natural Geisha Carbonic Maceration
coffees.description: If you know, you know and this coffee is truly something special! We were fortunate enough to receive a very limited quantity of this exceptional coffee. Once it’s gone, it’s gone! This coffee comes from a rock-star producer Jairo Arcila , and we couldn’t be more excited to share it with you. We had an incredible time cupping this beauty , and we hope you enjoy drinking it as much as we enjoyed tasting and…

coffees.title: Jairo Arcila Santa Monica Honey Pink Bourbon (Tartaric Acid / Cinnamon)
coffees.description: The ripe Pink Bourbon cherries undergo a dry anaerobic fermentation . During the fermentation, tartaric acid and organic cinnamon are introduced into the fermentation environment . Documented versions of this coffee report either 48 or 72 hours , depending on the specific lot. After fermentation, the cherries are pulped and the coffee is dried slowly on raised beds. The honey process does NOT mean honey is added .…

coffees.title: Jairo Arcila Santa Monica Washed Castillo (Wine Castillo / Lychee)
coffees.description: The Jairo Arcila Santa Monica Washed Castillo – Wine Yeast / Lychee is one of the more expressive co-fermented coffees from Finca Santa Monica. The ripe coffee cherries are carefully selected and fermented in a low-oxygen environment. During fermentation, lychee and wine yeast are added . After fermentation, the coffee is washed and dried on raised beds . That washed finish is important because it gives the coffee…

coffees.title: Mexico San Felipe Robusta Washed
coffees.description: Robusta has many attributes that often go overlooked. It contains nearly twice as much caffeine, has tons of body and from an agricultural standpoint, is significantly easier to grow and process. Despite that, we'll be honest, this coffee isn't meant to be enjoyed as a standalone cup. You can most certainly try it that way, especially if you've never tasted Robusta coffee before, but where it truly shines is as a…

coffees.title: Mexico Veracruz Finca La Laja
coffees.description: Grown in the mountain cloud forests of Veracruz, this coffee is tailor made for cool fall mornings. It's gently bright with a full body, creamy texture and a buttery yet clean finish. Look for notes of brown sugar, toffee, cashew and lemon meringue. A real crowd pleaser!

coffees.title: PERU Bourbon Anaerobic Washed - Germán Carranza Barboza
coffees.description: Germán picks ripe cherries and removes the floaters. He then places the cherries into a 50 gallon plastic tank, sealing it for three days (72 hours) to create the anaerobic effect. He then drives the coffee about an hour down to the valley by the Marañón River in the small village of Puerta Malleta where he shares a drying facility with his family. As opposed to at the farm, which is often subjected to heavy rains…

coffees.title: Panama Geisha Kalithea Coffee Estate
coffees.description: Kallithea, which means "beautiful view from the mountain" in Greek, is a farm located in the highlands of Volcan at the foot of the Baru volcano. Surrounded by tropical forests where lemon and citrus trees grow naturally, Kallithea cultivates Geisha, Pacamara, and Caturra varieties. Since the Caturra variety won the Traditional Washed category at the Best of Panama 2015, Kallithea's Caturra has boasted the highest…

coffees.title: Panama Los Gonzalez Anaerobic Natural
coffees.description: Don Mariano Coffee was named after Cafetalera Los González owner Mr. Mariano González. Mr. Mariano is a passionate coffee grower that has been taking care of his farm for the last 60 years. He is also a dear member of the Boquete community. Mr. Mariano, encouraged by his 3 daughters, joined the Specialty Coffee Association of Panama last year. He participated for the first time in the 2016 Best of Panama…

coffees.title: Papua New Guinea Arufa Natural Grade A
coffees.description: The Arufa Grade A Natural Process is grown in a remote area of Papua New Guinea in the Arufa and Kindeng regions of the Western Highlands. This area is a large plateau with stony mountains bordering the edges. During colonial times, this area was one of the first planted with coffee, and this continues today. Coffee in this area is mostly bourbon, Arusha, and blue mountain varieties and grows between 1,520 and…

coffees.title: Peru German Carranza Barboza Gesha Natural
coffees.description: Germán picks ripe cherries and removes the floaters. He then places the cherries into a 50 gallon plastic tank, sealing it for three days (72 hours) to create the anaerobic effect. He then drives the coffee about an hour down to the valley by the Marañón River in the small village of Puerta Malleta where he shares a drying facility with his family. As opposed to at the farm, which is often subjected to heavy rains…

coffees.title: Peru Junin Machu Picchu Organic
coffees.description: This community lot from the partner producers of Machu Picchu is a real crowd pleaser! It'll take on a variety of roasts well, it's excellent as a single origin or a blender and it's over all a very beginner friendly coffee to roast. Rich, creamy and balanced, in our cups we noted the sweetness of caramel and ripe red apple along with raisin and graham cracker.

coffees.title: Rwanda Regional Natural
coffees.description: This Natural coffee is produced by smallholders in Rwanda who deliver to RWACOF (Sucafina in Rwanda) washing stations. RWACOF’s Farmer Development Program in partnership with the London School of Economics (LSE) supports farmers with training in Good Agricultural Practices and access to loans, farm inputs and farm services. A new soil health initiative uses soil analysis data that RWACOF collected to identify farms…

coffees.title: Sebastian Gomez La Divisa Natural Gesha
coffees.description: If you know Gesha, you know this is a coffee worth paying attention to. Produced by Sebastián Gómez at his family farm, Finca La Divisa , in the highlands of Circasia, Quindío, Colombia, this 100% Gesha microlot represents the combination of exceptional genetics, high elevation, careful harvesting, and meticulous processing. The cherries are selectively hand-picked at peak ripeness and carefully sorted before being…

coffees.title: Sumatra Aceh Permata Gayo Mandheling
coffees.description: This Grade 1 offering comes to us from the Permata Gayo coop in the highlands of Aceh. It checks all the boxes we look for in a great Sumatran coffee: bold, rich, syrupy and earthy complexity, what more could you ask for? In the cup we got notes of luxurious pipe tobacco, toasted marshmallow, cacao nibs, a dash of pepper and even a touch of ripe plum.

coffees.title: Tanzania Nyasi Furaha Peaberry
coffees.description: This tasty offering from Southern Tanzania is an excellent representation of the classic Tanzania Peaberry profile. It's got gentle citric acidity, silky texture and subtle sweetness along with excellent balance and a clean, slightly floral finish. A very subtle coffee, don’t expect a blast of flavor! We noted lemon zest, buttery almond and amaretto, cherries, milk chocolate and a black tea undertone.

coffees.title: The Captain's House Blend
coffees.description: Our go-to, all purpose house blend. Big body, low acidity and smooth texture, it's sure to suit just about any coffee lover!

coffees.title: The Captain's Italian Blend
coffees.description: Experience the bold intensity, decadent chocolate undertones, and irresistibly smooth finish that define this classic espresso. Savor Italian coffee craftsmanship with every sip.

coffees.title: The Captain's Rico Amanecer Organic Blend
coffees.description: Awaken your senses with The Captain’s Rico Amanecer Organic Blend , a carefully crafted organic coffee designed to capture the warmth and promise of a new sunrise. "Amanecer," meaning sunrise, reflects the character of this blend comforting, vibrant, and full of life from the first sip to the last. This medium bodied blend delivers a warm, rich, and syrupy mouthfeel that coats the palate with exceptional sweetness…

coffees.title: Colombian Decaf EA Process
coffees.description: Colombian Decaf EA Process - This is a natural spring water – Ethyl Acetate (EA) combined process. This substance is obtained from the sugar cane industry around Palmira, Colombia and no chemicals are added to the beans. Hints of cocoa, with soft, fruity acidity. Balanced, medium body.
